glasses_felix: My previous note suggesting bed_b1 for late evening was incorrect for day 8. The item moved from bathroom_shelf_ba1 (08:12) to desk_b1 (21:39) and then to coffee_table_l1 (22:17). It does not stay in the bedroom. Check bathroom_shelf_ba1 for morning, desk_b1 for early evening, and coffee_table_l1 for late night. Do not default to bed_b1.

mug_felix: My previous note prioritizing kitchen_table_k1 was wrong for day 8. At 22:18, it was at coffee_table_l1, not desk_b1 or the kitchen. It appears to migrate to the living room in the evening. Check coffee_table_l1 for late-day queries. Avoid assuming it remains in the kitchen or bedroom desk without recent evidence.

glass_felix: My previous note to check kitchen_table_k1 before 23:00 was insufficient for day 8. At 22:59, it was already at cupboard_k1. The transition to the cupboard happens earlier than previously thought, or at least by the very end of the day. Check cupboard_k1 for any query after 22:00. Do not assume it is still on the kitchen table at 22:59.

water_bottle_felix: New pattern identified. At 21:08, it was at desk_b1, not kitchen_table_k1. This suggests a migration to the bedroom desk in the evening, similar to the tablet. Check desk_b1 for evening queries. Do not default to the kitchen table for late-day locations.

General Note: My assumption that Felix’s items follow static or simple kitchen-to-bedroom paths is flawed. The glasses and mug move to the living room (coffee table) in the late evening, not the bedroom. The glass moves to the cupboard earlier than expected. The water bottle moves to the bedroom desk. Always prioritize the most recent confirmed location over assumed daily cycles, as these items have distinct, non-uniform evening destinations.
